problem:
The volume of a right square pyramid is increasing. Given that its height $h$ is always twice the length of a base, find the rate of change of the volume of the pyramid with respect to its base length $s.$

*Hint*: The volume of a right square pyramid is $V=\frac{1}{3}{s}^{2}h.$

{{field-1}}.

feedback.problem:
In an acoustics lab, the ambient noise power (in decibels) at frequency $f$ (in $\text{kHz}$) is modeled by the function

$$
N(f)={2}^{-2{f}^{2}}.
$$

What is the exact value of the instantaneous rate at which the noise power is changing with respect to frequency when $f=2\,\text{kHz}?$ 

The instantaneous rate of change when $f=2\,\text{kHz}$ is 
{{field-1}} decibels per $\text{kHz}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The instantaneous rate of change at which the ambient noise power is changing when $f=2$ kHz is equal to ${N}^{′}(2).$

Taking the derivative, the rate of change of $N(f)$ with respect to $f$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{N}^{′}(f) & =\frac{d}{df}({2}^{-2{f}^{2}}) \\  & ={2}^{-2{f}^{2}}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\cdot (-4f) \\  & =-4f\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\,{2}^{-2{f}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

and evaluating at $f=2$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{N}^{′}(2) & =-4(2)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\,{2}^{-2(2)^{2}} \\  & =-8\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\,{2}^{-8} \\  & =-\frac{8\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}{256} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}{32}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate at which the ambient noise power is changing when $f=2\,\text{kHz}$ is $-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}{32}$ decibels per $\text{kHz}.$
